summary: Two parts: Lemuel's mother's advice to king (not give strength to women, wine to kings, speak for those without voice), then acrostic poem of woman of valor (eshet chayil) — trustworthy, works with hands, rises before dawn, buys field, clothes household scarlet, strength and dignity, opens mouth with wisdom, kindness, fears Yahweh, children and husband praise her.
whyItMatters: Often misused as checklist for women; originally praise poem for woman's wisdom, enterprise, and fear of Yahweh — not perfection but multi-faceted strength. Ends Proverbs where book began seeking wisdom — now embodied in woman.

context.author: Lemuel and anonymous acrostic poet
context.literaryForm: King's oracle + alphabetic acrostic (22 verses each starting with Hebrew alphabet)

outline.heading: Lemuel's mother's oracle — not for kings wine, strong drink, speak for poor and needy
Woman of valor acrostic — who can find? Far more than rubies
outline.note: Hands, trading, field, lamp, wisdom, fear of Yahweh

keyVerses.text: Who can find a worthy woman? For her value is far above rubies.
Strength and dignity are her clothing. She laughs at the time to come.
keyVerses.why: Strength + wisdom + laughter at future — not anxious.

keyVerses.text: Charm is deceitful, and beauty is vain; but a woman who fears Yahweh, she shall be praised.
keyVerses.why: Climax — what endures is fear of Yahweh, not charm/beauty.

questions.question: Is Proverbs 31 a checklist for women to feel guilty?
questions.answer: No — acrostic poem is idealized portrait, like superhero, not daily to-do list. One woman can't do all in one day: buys field, makes clothes, trades, teaches, at night. It's 22 verses covering seasons of life, not 24 hours. Originally, Jewish tradition has husband and children sing it to wife/mother on Sabbath as praise, not pressure. Ends 'give her fruit of hands' — community praises her.

questions.question: What does 'woman of valor / eshet chayil' mean?
questions.answer: Chayil = valor, strength, military might, wealth, capability — same word for mighty men of valor. Not meek or merely nice; strong, capable, enterprising. Valor includes economic (buys field, trades), managerial (household), compassionate (opens hand to poor v20), intellectual (mouth wisdom).

questions.question: Why does it say 'her husband is known in gates' where elders sit?
questions.answer: City gate is where elders judged and commerce happened — husband respected partly because household runs well due to her work. Not that she is invisible; her work enables his public role. Mutual honor, not one-sided subservience.

questions.question: What about verses 3-7 — wine and strong drink not for kings?
questions.answer: First part from mother to King Lemuel: kings shouldn't drink heavily lest they forget law and pervert justice for afflicted, and don't give strength to women who destroy kings (like power misuse). Instead, give strong drink to those perishing — possibly medicinal. Then commands: speak up for those without voice, judge justly, defend poor needy — advocacy is royal duty.

questions.question: What does 'strength and dignity are her clothing, she laughs at time to come' mean?
questions.answer: Clothing metaphor: earlier she clothes household scarlet, herself with fine linen; here strength and dignity are her garment — what she wears. Laughs at future = not anxious about coming days because prepared, wise, trusting. Wisdom literature says fear of Yahweh is beginning of wisdom — ends with that (v30).

glossary.def: Woman of valor/strength — same word used for mighty warriors.
Poem where each verse starts with successive letter of alphabet — 22 verses for 22 Hebrew letters.
Reverent awe, trust, beginning of wisdom — not terror.
